sources.publisher: Office of the President of the Czech Republic
sources.title: Petr Pavel: official Czech biography
sources.findings: Read the Czech presidential biography: born 1 November 1961 in Planá near Mariánské Lázně; military college graduation 1983, postgraduate intelligence study in Brno, and MA in international relations at King’s College London in 2006. It acknowledges Communist Party membership in 1985–1989 and entry to the General Staff intelligence administration in 1988. Its shorthand of NATO election in 2015 conflicts with the precise September 2014 election in NATO and defence records; the profile distinguishes election from June 2015 assumption of office. The rescue total of 53 differs from the Czech Radio profile’s 33, so no number is published. Its broad narrative ordering is not used to date the UNPROFOR rescue after the Belgian attaché post. The biography also supports the 2020 fundraising initiative and 6 September 2022 candidacy.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Defence of the Czech Republic
sources.title: General Petr Pavel: historical military biography
sources.findings: Read the defence ministry’s historical biography: military college 1979–1983, postgraduate study 1988–1991, British courses and King’s College study in 2005–2006. It dates chief-of-staff service to 1 July 2012–30 April 2015 and NATO election to 20 September 2014 in Vilnius. NATO prose says the national post ended in May 2015; the profile uses spring 2015 rather than pretending this precision difference is resolved. The ministry’s brigadier promotion date of 12 December 2002 differs from 1 December in other official biographies and is not used. Historical page headings do not establish a current military appointment.

sources.title: General Petr Pavel: Chair of the Military Committee, June 2015–June 2018
sources.findings: Read NATO biography and service table: elected chair on 20 September 2014, took office on 26 June 2015, term June 2015–June 2018. The role is military advice and committee leadership, not NATO Secretary General or Supreme Allied Commander Europe. Birth and education corroborate presidential records. Its 1985–1991 company-command span is broader than the presidency’s 1985–1988 command plus 1988–1991 study sequence; no unsupported uninterrupted command claim is made. National military representation at US CENTCOM is not US military command. Login-interface text on the page did not block the public biography; no authentication was attempted.

sources.title: Petr Pavel: military career and January 1993 rescue, 26 April 2018
sources.findings: Read Military History Institute Prague article of 26 April 2018: birth and military schooling, international-relations study, UNPROFOR operation in January 1993 to evacuate a French unit under fire, and subsequent French Croix de Guerre. It supports the event without supplying a disputed rescue total. It also confirms 2014 NATO election versus June 2015 assumption. Its description of a future June 2018 successor was a contemporary forecast, not evidence of 2026 office or activity.

sources.title: Second-round presidential election result, 28 January 2023
sources.findings: Read Czech Statistical Office release of 28 January 2023: Pavel won the second round with 58.32% and Babiš received 41.67%; 5,759,197 valid votes and 70.25% turnout are separate quantities. The percentage refers to valid runoff votes, not all eligible voters, total population, the first round or parliamentary seats. The release said the electoral commission would meet on Monday; no same-day completion of that later approval is inferred. No ballot-level dataset or separate commission decision was inspected.

sources.title: Petr Pavel takes the presidential oath, 9 March 2023
sources.findings: Read the government’s 9 March 2023 inauguration article, reached from its photo-gallery link: Pavel took the oath at a joint meeting of both parliamentary chambers in Vladislav Hall and succeeded Miloš Zeman. Election victory on 28 January is distinct from taking office on 9 March. Fiala’s positive assessment of the incoming president is political commentary, not independently measured presidential performance. Gallery captions were read, not original photographs.

sources.title: Pavel discusses ammunition procurement and financing in Munich, 17 February 2024
sources.findings: Read ČT24/ČTK report of 17 February 2024 on the Munich Security Conference. Pavel identified possible procurement of 500,000 rounds of 155 mm and 300,000 rounds of 122 mm ammunition and sought partner financing. This was an availability and funding announcement, not proof all 800,000 rounds were delivered. The report attributes statements to Pavel and Defence Minister Černochová. No specific supplier countries, completed contract value, later delivery tally or independent audit is inferred from the announcement. Embedded videos were not viewed.

sources.title: Presidential candidate profile, 25 November 2022; updated 14 January 2023
sources.findings: Read Czech Radio’s candidate profile, published 25 November 2022 and updated 14 January 2023. It corroborates birth, Communist Party membership in 1985–1989, intelligence training, retirement in 2018, the 2020 initiative and 6 September 2022 campaign announcement. His stated regret is attributed to him. The report mentions a negative lustration certificate; the original certificate and intelligence archives were not examined, and no criminal finding is inferred. Its rescued-soldier total of 33 conflicts with the presidency’s 53. Its January first-round result is not the eventual 58.32% runoff result. The site’s 2026 header date is not the article’s update date.

sources.title: Interview with Petr Pavel on Národní třída, 17 November 2026
sources.findings: Read the 17 November 2026 Radiožurnál/iROZHLAS interview, published at 11:20, including the reported visit to Národní třída and his answers on domestic protest and government responsibility. It establishes actual public activity on the remembrance day. He expressly said he followed the earlier Letná demonstration at home; he is not recorded as attending that protest. Interviewer descriptions of protest size, political demands and planned international meetings are not independently certified outcomes. Original audio was not heard.

sources.publisher: Office of the President of the Czech Republic
sources.title: Meeting with the Hungarian president, 10 November 2026
sources.findings: Read the presidential office release of 10 November 2026 confirming Pavel and Eva Pavlová welcomed Hungarian President András Baka and Katalin Kövesdi at Prague Castle. Discussed topics were nuclear energy, EU external borders and European industrial competitiveness. This supports a completed meeting, not a new binding treaty, completed project or independently demonstrated economic outcome. The 2026 counterpart names are taken from the dated release; no older officeholder is substituted.
